Co-facilitate two-hour governance lab sessions with small groups of community members at CUNY SPH in Harlem for Locally Informed Futures for Health Equity (LIFHE), a two-year project developing a community-centered governance framework for health AI, run in partnership with the Harlem Health Initiative at CUNY SPH. Two openings.

Qualifications — applicants should:
- Be an alum or graduate student at CUNY SPH in good academic standing
- Have experience facilitating groups, workshops, or community meetings, and be comfortable facilitating discussion among people with different perspectives
- Be available for sessions at CUNY SPH in Harlem on Wednesday afternoons and early evenings
- Demonstrate clear, plain-language writing skills
- Have an interest in health equity, community engagement or participatory research, and governance of digital health technologies and AI (technical AI background NOT required)
- Have strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple moving pieces
- Be able to complete CITI human subjects research training before session-based activities

Coursework in community engagement, participatory research, qualitative analysis, or project management is welcome but not required.

Responsibilities: co-facilitate alongside a project team member using a prepared guide; team prep meetings and independent review of facilitation guides; team debriefs plus written debriefs; session logistics, materials, room setup, participant welcome; structured session summaries and handoff of drafted governance language. Project coordination: session scheduling and participant confirmations across three participant groups, timeline and action-item tracking, project management and audit-trail systems, recruitment support with the Harlem Health Initiative and CBO partners.
1700000073000.notes:
Found on Handshake (CUNY SPH board) 8/27/26. TOP-RATED of the Handshake batch — best hours-to-value ratio in the pipeline.

EFFECTIVE HOURLY: $56-100/hr, midpoint ~$73/hr. The 5-6 hrs/week figure applies to weeks that HAVE a session, not every week of the semester — the posting says to expect heavier weeks around sessions and lighter weeks between, and ~5 hrs of intern time per session matches. So 4-6 sessions at 5-6 hrs = 20-36 hrs total for the semester ($100/hr at 20 hrs, $55.56/hr at 36 hrs), averaging about 2 hrs/week across Sept 1-Dec 18. This is 2.5-3.4x the CUNY K-16 rate of $29.32 and the highest effective rate in the pipeline. Worth confirming expected total hours at interview, but the reading is well supported by the posting. Watch for scope creep from the open-ended coordination duties (scheduling across three participant groups, timeline tracking, audit-trail systems, recruitment support) pushing actual hours past the session-based estimate.

SCHEDULE CONFIRMED CLEAR: fall classes meet Tuesday and Thursday late afternoons, in person at CUNY SPH — the same building as the sessions. Wednesday afternoons and early evenings do not conflict. Note one course has weekly assignments due Wednesday nights, so session days double as submission days. Onsite ~3 hrs per session, everything else remote.

APPLY TO info@healthjustice.co with resume and cover letter. The cover letter MUST describe a group, workshop, or meeting she has facilitated and what she learned — her closest evidence is partner office hours, training/TA delivery at United Way, and 15+ community intake events. DO NOT send a writing sample initially; candidates invited to interview provide up to two pages written for a general or community audience, not academic. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis with interviews beginning immediately, so the real deadline is earlier than the 8/31/26 Handshake cutoff in closeDate.

STACKABLE: at roughly 2 hrs/week averaged across the semester this is additive, not a substitute — applicant's own read is that it is reasonable to hold alongside a part-time or even a full-time job. Do NOT treat it as competing with the full-time search; it should run in parallel with whatever lands. This is the only Handshake find in the batch that stacks; Citymeals (20 hrs/wk), Oaklin Lane (25 hrs/wk), NYHF (9-month part-time), and CUNY K-16 (19 hrs/wk) all require a job-sized opening in the schedule.

UPSIDE: continuing into Spring 2027 may include community-based qualitative analysis, codebook development, coding, and contributing to peer-reviewed papers and policy briefs. Health Justice was founded by Dr. Oni Blackstock.

scoreRationale.qualification: Clears the hard gate outright — CUNY SPH graduate student — and the pool is restricted to CUNY SPH people, which narrows the field sharply. Facilitation experience is the listed soft spot; office hours, trainings, and community intake events are defensible but she needs one specific story for the cover letter.
scoreRationale.enjoyment: Participant-facing, which normally scores down, but it is co-facilitated from a prepared guide alongside a project team member, and the hours-to-stipend ratio makes it worth it on her own assessment.
scoreRationale.school: Confirmed against the Fall 2026 syllabi: classes are Tuesday and Thursday 4-5:50pm, so Wednesday afternoon and early evening sessions are clear. Easiest schedule fit anywhere in the pipeline.
scoreRationale.location: Sessions are at the CUNY SPH building in Harlem where she already attends class, so there is no additional commute.
scoreRationale.mph: Health equity, community governance, and AI in health is current, publishable subject matter directly inside her degree.
scoreRationale.mission: Community-centered health equity research in Harlem, led by a physician-founder, is a strong mission match.
